sentences.en: Hi, this is Kim Mills, host of Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是金·米尔斯，《心理学话语》栏目主持人。

sentences.en: Today, we're sharing an episode from another podcast that we think you'll enjoy,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将分享来自另一个我们认为你会喜欢的播客节目中的一集，

sentences.en: Call to Mind from American Public Media.
sentences.zh: 它是由美国公共传媒制作的《清醒时刻》。

sentences.en: Call to Mind is American Public Media's initiative to foster new conversations about mental health.
sentences.zh: 《清醒时刻》是美国公共传媒的一项旨在激发关于心理健康新对话的倡议。

sentences.en: This episode, The Strain of Stress, looks at the many pressures Americans are facing today, from financial worries to political division,
sentences.zh: 本期节目《压力的重担》探讨了美国人今天面临的种种压力，从财务担忧到政治分歧，

sentences.en: how chronic stress can affect both mental and physical health, and how to manage the strain.
sentences.zh: 慢性压力如何影响心理和身体健康，以及如何应对这种压力。

sentences.en: You'll hear from two familiar voices, Arthur C.
sentences.zh: 你将听到两个熟悉的声音，小亚瑟·C·

sentences.en: Evans Jr.,
sentences.zh: 埃文斯，

sentences.en: CEO of the American Psychological Association, and Dennis Stolle, APA's Head of Applied Psychology.
sentences.zh: 美国心理学会首席执行官，以及APA应用心理学部负责人丹尼斯·斯托尔。

sentences.en: If you enjoy this episode, you can find more from the Call to Mind team at calltomindenow.org or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这集节目，你可以在calltomindenow.org或你获取播客的任何地方找到更多来自《清醒时刻》团队的内容。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoy this episode.
sentences.zh: 我们希望你喜欢这集节目。

sentences.en: You're listening to The Strain of Stress, a special report from Call to Mind,
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《压力的重担》，这是来自《清醒时刻》的特别报道，

sentences.en: American Public Media's initiative to foster new conversations about mental health.
sentences.zh: 这是美国公共传媒旨在引发关于心理健康新对话的倡议。

sentences.en: I'm Angela Davis.
sentences.zh: 我是安吉拉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: What stresses me out?
sentences.zh: 什么让我感到压力？

sentences.en: I think, like most people, current times are very stressful.
sentences.zh: 我想，就像大多数人一样，现在的时期压力非常大。

sentences.en: This is Gina Marie, a New Yorker who generously agreed to share her experiences with stress.
sentences.zh: 这是吉娜·玛丽，一位慷慨同意分享她压力经历的纽约人。

sentences.en: As a Black woman, a middle-aged Black woman, I do not feel protected at all.
sentences.zh: 作为一个黑人女性，一个中年黑人女性，我完全感觉不到保护。

sentences.en: I wake up in the morning almost with a coat of armor that I need to put on before I leave my house.
sentences.zh: 我早上醒来，几乎就像穿了一件盔甲，在我离开家之前必须穿上它。

sentences.en: I think that that just sets the foundation of stress even before I get to work.
sentences.zh: 我认为这甚至在我去上班之前就奠定了压力的基础。

sentences.en: Experts who study stress say it's deeply personal.
sentences.zh: 研究压力的专家表示，压力是非常个人化的。

sentences.en: And what stresses us can seem big or small.
sentences.zh: 而让我们感到压力的事可大可小。

sentences.en: But almost anything can cause a person to feel stress.
sentences.zh: 但几乎任何事都能让人感到压力。

sentences.en: And now work is another circumstance.
sentences.zh: 现在工作成了另一种情况。

sentences.en: You know, the company I work for just laid off almost 15,000 people, I believe it was.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我工作的公司刚刚裁员了将近1.5万人，我想是这样的。

sentences.en: Those of us who are left behind feel a great deal of stress.
sentences.zh: 我们这些留下来的人感到巨大的压力。

sentences.en: And that my day could end at any moment.
sentences.zh: 而我的日子可能随时结束。

sentences.en: You know, as a mom, that makes me nervous.
sentences.zh: 你知道，作为一个妈妈，这让我感到紧张。

sentences.en: Gina Marie's family stress is real.
sentences.zh: 吉娜·玛丽的家庭压力是真实的。

sentences.en: She and her husband are foster parents on the way to adoption.
sentences.zh: 她和她的丈夫正在收养孩子的路上担任寄养父母。

sentences.en: And their case has been going for years.
sentences.zh: 他们的案子已经持续了好几年。

sentences.en: She says the love she feels for her kids is incredible.
sentences.zh: 她说她对孩子们的爱是不可思议的。

sentences.en: But it can't erase how overwhelming the journey has been.
sentences.zh: 但它无法抹去这段旅程有多么令人窒息。

sentences.en: I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道。

sentences.en: I was naive, admittedly, about the emotional toll, the marital toll, the everything toll that it takes.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我曾天真地以为，它带来的情感代价、婚姻代价、一切代价是如此巨大。

sentences.en: Just being in it now has presented several years of stress that I had not imagined I'd be having at this point in my life.
sentences.zh: 身处其中让我经历了几年我从未想过在人生这个阶段会有的压力。

sentences.en: Being middle-aged and perimenopausal, which is another set of stress.
sentences.zh: 身为中年并处于围绝经期，这是另一层压力。

sentences.en: Gina Marie's story shares something common about stress.
sentences.zh: 吉娜·玛丽的故事反映了关于压力的一个普遍现象。

sentences.en: It's rare for us to deal with one demanding thing at a time.
sentences.zh: 我们很少同时只应付一件棘手的事。

sentences.en: Typically, there are many.
sentences.zh: 通常有很多件。

sentences.en: And there's usually some nuance to what stresses us.
sentences.zh: 而且让我们感到压力的东西往往有些微妙之处。

sentences.en: For example, it's great to have family and friends, but sometimes family and friends are stressful.
sentences.zh: 例如，有家人和朋友很好，但有时家人和朋友也很有压力。

sentences.en: One thing is certain, we all have stress.
sentences.zh: 有一点是肯定的，我们都有压力。

sentences.en: And we can feel it.
sentences.zh: 我们能感觉得到。

sentences.en: Think about situations where your heart starts to pound or your mind begins to race.
sentences.zh: 想想那些心跳加速或大脑飞转的时刻。

sentences.en: Maybe your palms get sweaty or you feel like you are carrying an invisible weight.
sentences.zh: 也许你手心出汗，或者感觉自己背负着无形的重担。

sentences.en: These are natural responses to stress, and they can overwhelm us.
sentences.zh: 这些都是对压力的自然反应，它们可能会让我们不堪重负。

sentences.en: National surveys confirm people in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 全国性调查证实，自2020年新冠疫情爆发以来，美国人

sentences.en: have experienced historic levels of stress since the COVID-19 pandemic started in 2020.
sentences.zh: 经历了历史最高水平的压力。

sentences.en: And what stresses us out ranges from personal pressures, like money and jobs, to large societal issues like politics or the impact of racism.
sentences.zh: 而让我们感到压力的事物从金钱和工作等个人压力，到政治或种族主义影响等大型社会问题不等。

sentences.en: Experts warn that living with so much stress doesn't just make us feel bad in the moment.
sentences.zh: 专家警告说，带着如此巨大的压力生活不仅会让我们当下感觉糟糕。

sentences.en: It can cause serious health issues.
sentences.zh: 它还会导致严重的健康问题。

sentences.en: Chronic stress puts us more at risk for a mental illness or a substance use disorder.
sentences.zh: 慢性压力使我们更有可能患上精神疾病或物质使用障碍。

sentences.en: This report is about stress, the kinds of stress that we all deal with by just being alive.
sentences.zh: 本报道关于压力，即我们仅仅作为生命活着就要应对的各种压力。

sentences.en: We won't cover trauma or post-traumatic stress disorder in this program, but we will talk about the everyday issues that overwhelm us and the impact of stress on our well-being.
sentences.zh: 我们在本节目中不会涉及创伤或创伤后应激障碍，但我们会讨论那些让我们不堪重负的日常问题以及压力对我们福祉的影响。

sentences.en: I'll also talk with experts seeking solutions and get tips on how to best manage stress.
sentences.zh: 我还将与寻求解决方案的专家交谈，并获得如何最好地管理压力的建议。

sentences.en: Let's start with Dr. Arthur Evans Jr.
sentences.zh: 让我们从华盛顿特区的亚瑟·埃文斯博士开始。

sentences.en: in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿特区

sentences.en: He's a clinical and community psychologist and currently the CEO of the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 他是一名临床和社区心理学家，目前担任美国心理学会首席执行官。

sentences.en: Dr. Evans says stress isn't inherently a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 埃文斯博士表示，压力本质上并非坏事。

sentences.en: It can actually be useful.
sentences.zh: 它其实很有用。

sentences.en: Stress actually helps us when we need to be motivated to do something.
sentences.zh: 当我们因需要做某事而获得动力时，压力实际上对我们有帮助。

sentences.en: The problem is when that stress is very acute or when it's very intense or when we are dealing with it over a very long period of time.
sentences.zh: 问题在于压力非常急性、非常强烈，或者我们长期与之对抗的时候。

sentences.en: That's when we really have to worry about stress in our lives.
sentences.zh: 那才是我们真正需要担心生活中压力的时候。

sentences.en: And there are different kinds of stress, too.
sentences.zh: 而且压力也有不同的种类。

sentences.en: There are absolutely different kinds of stress.
sentences.zh: 确实有不同种类的压力。

sentences.en: There's certainly stress that is caused by psychological issues that could be a relationship,
sentences.zh: 当然有由心理问题引起的压力，可能是人际关系，

sentences.en: that could be just dealing with what people are seeing happening in the world around us.
sentences.zh: 可能只是应对人们在身边世界看到的事情。

sentences.en: There's stress that's related to our ability to actually get things done.
sentences.zh: 有与我们实际完成任务能力相关的压力。

sentences.en: I'll tell you, when I was in graduate school, the stress that I looked at was economic stress.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你，我在读研究生时，我关注的压力是经济压力。

sentences.en: Economic stressors can cause significant psychological distress.
sentences.zh: 经济压力源会导致显著的心理困扰。

sentences.en: So when we see, for example, the economy have a downturn, we will also see an increase in the number of people coming into treatment.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们看到经济下滑时，我们也会看到前来接受治疗的人数增加。

sentences.en: Dr. Arthur Evans Jr.
sentences.zh: 小亚瑟·埃文斯博士

sentences.en: says there are two main kinds of stress, acute stress and chronic stress.
sentences.zh: 表示主要有两种压力，急性压力和慢性压力。

sentences.en: Acute stress is something that's short-term.
sentences.zh: 急性压力是短期的。

sentences.en: It comes and goes quickly, like a difficult exam at school or getting stuck in traffic when you're running late.
sentences.zh: 它来得快去得也快，比如学校里的困难考试，或者快迟到时被困在交通堵塞中。

sentences.en: But chronic stress is long-term.
sentences.zh: 但慢性压力是长期的。

sentences.en: It can last months or even years.
sentences.zh: 它可以持续数月甚至数年。

sentences.en: Living with relentless financial problems or caring for a really sick family member.
sentences.zh: 生活在无休止的财务问题中，或者照顾重病的家庭成员。

sentences.en: Dr. Evans says chronic stress can trigger serious health issues.
sentences.zh: 埃文斯博士说，慢性压力会引发严重的健康问题。

sentences.en: And you might start to recognize it's a problem when your work or your everyday activities get unusually challenging.
sentences.zh: 当你的工作或日常生活变得异常具有挑战性时，你可能会开始意识到这是一个问题。

sentences.en: And so what you start to see is problems in your activities of daily living.
sentences.zh: 所以你开始看到的是日常生活活动中的问题。

sentences.en: So if you're a parent, you start to see you're not on top of your parenting.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你是一位父母，你会发现你无法很好地抚养孩子。

sentences.en: If you're a worker, you're starting to see that your work is slipping.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一名员工，你会发现你的工作效率在下滑。

sentences.en: So the issue for us is really, one, making sure that we understand what are the signs that we are stressed.
sentences.zh: 所以对我们来说，问题实际上在于，第一，确保我们了解我们感到压力的迹象是什么。

sentences.en: I'll give you an example.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个例子。

sentences.en: One of the things that I know about me, I'm a pretty optimistic person.
sentences.zh: 我对自己了解的一点是，我是一个相当乐观的人。

sentences.en: And when I start to get cynical, I know that that's because I'm feeling stressed.
sentences.zh: 当我开始变得愤世嫉俗时，我知道那是因为我感到压力。

sentences.en: And so I've come to know that if I start to get a little cynical, I start to pay attention to, OK, so what's going on with me?
sentences.zh: 所以我逐渐了解到，如果我开始变得有点愤世嫉俗，我就会开始关注：好吧，我身上发生了什么？

sentences.en: Why am I feeling stressed?
sentences.zh: 为什么我感到压力？

sentences.en: And then I can take steps to deal with that.
sentences.zh: 然后我可以采取步骤来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So what are some common mental illnesses that stress can actually trigger?
sentences.zh: 那么压力实际上会引发哪些常见的精神疾病呢？

sentences.en: Certainly substance use, people can start drinking or using drugs as a way of managing their stress.
sentences.zh: 当然是物质使用，人们可能会开始喝酒或吸毒，以此作为管理压力的一种方式。

sentences.en: One can become depressed.
sentences.zh: 人可能会陷入抑郁。

sentences.en: You know, post-traumatic stress syndrome is an anxiety disorder that is caused by experiencing a traumatic event that was overwhelming to the person
sentences.zh: 你知道，创伤后应激综合征是一种焦虑症，由经历对个人而言过于沉重的创伤事件引起，

sentences.en: and having a stress reaction in relationship to how they recover and deal with that particular traumatic event.
sentences.zh: 并且在如何恢复和应对该特定创伤事件方面产生应激反应。

sentences.en: Dr. Evans says someone living with chronic stress is more likely to develop cardiovascular problems, type 2 diabetes, or a dangerously weakened immune system.
sentences.zh: 埃文斯博士说，生活在慢性压力中的人更有可能患上心血管疾病、2型糖尿病或危险的免疫系统受损。

sentences.en: It can also make existing mental health conditions worse.
sentences.zh: 它还会使现有的心理健康状况恶化。

sentences.en: For nearly 20 years, the American Psychological Association has published an annual report called Stress in America.
sentences.zh: 近20年来，美国心理学会每年都会发布一份名为《美国压力》的年度报告。

sentences.en: It's a national study about what's stressing out people in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这是一项关于美国人压力来源的全国性研究。

sentences.en: And this year, half of the folks who participated said societal division stresses them out, and they feel more isolated because of it.
sentences.zh: 而今年，一半的参与者表示社会分歧让他们感到压力，他们因此感到更加孤立。

sentences.en: Here's Dr. Evans.
sentences.zh: 请听埃文斯博士的讲述。

sentences.en: We know that social connection is enormously important to our health, probably one of the strongest predictors of how well we do in life.
sentences.zh: 我们知道社会联系对我们的健康极其重要，可能是我们在生活中过得好坏的最强大预测指标之一。

sentences.en: And what we're seeing is that the stressors, particularly around the social divide, are leading to people disconnecting from relationships that they have historically had.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是，压力源，特别是围绕社会分歧的压力源，正导致人们与他们历来拥有的关系断开连接。

sentences.en: And we know that when people are less connected, that it leads to a whole variety of challenges.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，当人们的联系减少时，会导致各种各样的挑战。

sentences.en: Loneliness can have a tremendous impact on our health status, both our psychological health and our physical health.
sentences.zh: 孤独会对我们的健康状况产生巨大影响，包括心理健康和身体健康。

sentences.en: And so if we look at stress from purely the standpoint of the stressors that we're experiencing are only affecting the individual, what we're seeing is, no,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们纯粹从我们经历的压力源只影响个人的角度来看待压力，我们看到的却是，不，

sentences.en: it's affecting all of us.
sentences.zh: 它影响着我们所有人。

sentences.en: And it's affecting how we then relate to each other.
sentences.zh: 它影响着我们彼此之间的交往方式。

sentences.en: And to the degree that we are more disconnected, that, in fact, exacerbates the impact that stress can have in our lives.
sentences.zh: 从我们的联系越发断开的程度上来说，这实际上会加剧压力在我们生活中产生的影响。

sentences.en: Yes, the words societal division is in there a lot.
sentences.zh: 是的，“社会分歧”这个词在里面出现了很多次。

sentences.en: But, you know, an interesting finding, 62 percent of adults in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，一个有趣的发现是，62%的美国成年人

sentences.en: reported societal division was a significant source of stress in their lives.
sentences.zh: 报告称社会分歧是他们生活中压力的重要来源。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that was really surprising.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的很令人惊讶。

sentences.en: If you think about this, half of Americans are feeling lonely and disconnected.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，一半的美国人感到孤独和脱节。

sentences.en: That is just an astounding number that that many Americans are feeling like they don't have the adequate support.
sentences.zh: 如此多的美国人觉得自己没有获得足够的支援，这个数字实在是惊人的。

sentences.en: Those relationships are what keeps us healthy.
sentences.zh: 这些关系正是让我们保持健康的秘诀。

sentences.en: Those are the things that are most related to our health status.
sentences.zh: 这些是与我们健康状况最息息相关的因素。

sentences.en: When we think about what's at stake when people are increasingly stressed about society, politics and the nation, how can that show up?
sentences.zh: 当我们思考当人们对社会、政治和国家感到越来越大压力时，到底有什么风险，这会如何表现出来？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, one of the ways is that we stop trusting people who we should be in a more trusting relationship with.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，其中一种表现形式是我们停止信任那些我们本应建立更信任关系的人。

sentences.en: You know, society works when there is some level of truSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，社会运作的基础是某种程度的信任。

sentences.en: You trust the person who's teaching your child.
sentences.zh: 你信任教你孩子的人。

sentences.en: You trust the health care provider that you're going to.
sentences.zh: 你信任为你服务的医疗保健提供者。

sentences.en: You trust your colleague.
sentences.zh: 你信任你的同事。

sentences.en: When that starts to break down, it really impacts a lot of areas of our society.
sentences.zh: 当这种信任开始崩溃时，它确实会严重影响我们社会的许多领域。

sentences.en: And I think all of us then need to be concerned when we know that there are these issues that are in our society that are leading to not only this disconnection,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们所有人都需要关切的是，我们知道社会中存在的这些问题不仅导致了这种脱节，

sentences.en: but this erosion of trust between one another.
sentences.zh: 还导致了彼此之间信任的侵蚀。

sentences.en: That's Dr. Arthur Evans, Jr.
sentences.zh: 这是来自美国心理学会的小亚瑟·埃文斯博士。

sentences.en: from the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 来自美国心理学会

sentences.en: You're listening to The Strain of Stress, a special report from Call to Mind.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《压力的重担》，来自《清醒时刻》的特别报道。

sentences.en: I'm Angela Davis.
sentences.zh: 我是安吉拉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: As we heard from Dr. Evans, political division is a significant source of stress for adults in the United States.
sentences.zh: 正如我们从埃文斯博士那里听到的，政治分歧是美国成年人压力的重要来源。

sentences.en: And if it feels like we are less politically united, that's true.
sentences.zh: 如果我们觉得我们在政治上更加不团结了，那是真的。

sentences.en: And there's even some data to back it up.
sentences.zh: 甚至有一些数据可以支持这一点。

sentences.en: A long-running survey conducted by the University of Michigan, Stanford,
sentences.zh: 密歇根大学、斯坦福大学

sentences.en: and other universities found that Americans give their opposing political party the lowest approval rating since the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 和其他大学进行的一项长期调查发现，美国人对反对党的好感度降到了20世纪60年代以来的最低点。

sentences.en: And these political rifts are fracturing some friendships and families.
sentences.zh: 这些政治裂痕正在撕裂一些友谊和家庭。

sentences.en: Reporter Chris Benderer has more.
sentences.zh: 记者克里斯·本德勒带来了更多报道。

sentences.en: This story begins where so much political division begins, on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 这个故事始于许多政治分歧开始的地方，即Facebook。

sentences.en: In this case, with a woman named Sarah.
sentences.zh: 在这个案例中，主角是一位名叫莎拉的女性。

sentences.en: We're not using her last name for privacy reasons.
sentences.zh: 出于隐私原因，我们没有使用她的姓氏。

sentences.en: Anyway, Sarah works as a Spanish interpreter.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，莎拉是一名西班牙语口译员。

sentences.en: And way back in 2015, she got one of her most exciting assignments ever.
sentences.zh: 早在2015年，她接到了她有生以来最令人兴奋的任务之一。

sentences.en: And I was, you know, basically saying I'm really proud of myself.
sentences.zh: 我当时，你知道，基本上是在说我为自己感到非常骄傲。

sentences.en: Today was a really important moment.
sentences.zh: 今天是极其重要的一刻。

sentences.en: I got to interpret for Michelle Obama.
sentences.zh: 我得以担任米歇尔·奥巴马的口译。

sentences.en: I mean, it was just, you know, me tooting my horn a little bit that I had gotten to meet her and got to interpret for her.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这只是，你知道，我稍微自吹自擂一下，说我见到了她并为她做了口译。

sentences.en: Sarah's a Democrat, but she says the post was not explicitly political.
sentences.zh: 莎拉是一名民主党人，但她说这篇帖子并非明确的政治贴。

sentences.en: I checked, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我查过了。

sentences.en: The entire post was one sentence.
sentences.zh: 整篇帖子只有一句话。

sentences.en: Quote,
sentences.zh: 他说：

sentences.en: But soon, a lot of people Sarah knew started commenting under the post about their dislike for Michelle Obama and President Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 但不久之后，萨拉认识的许多人开始在帖子下方留言，表达他们对米歇尔·奥巴马和巴拉克·奥巴马总统的不满。

sentences.en: And their dislike that Sarah had gone to the Obama White House.
sentences.zh: 以及对萨拉去过奥巴马白宫的不满。

sentences.en: Now, Sarah grew up in a fairly conservative part of Colorado.
sentences.zh: 萨拉在科罗拉多州一个相当保守的地区长大。

sentences.en: She disagreed with people from her hometown online for years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，她在网上与家乡的人意见不合。

sentences.en: But still, she was disheartened at how quickly a few of her friends had made things contentious.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，她还是感到沮丧，因为她的几个朋友这么快就把事情搞得充满敌意。

sentences.en: I did respond in my response with something along the lines of, it's really sad that you can't even be proud of me for an accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 我在回复中确实写了一些类似这样的话：真让人难过，你甚至不能为我取得的成就感到骄傲。

sentences.en: And then I did quietly unfriend them.
sentences.zh: 然后我默默地把他们取消好友了。

sentences.en: I called up Sarah to talk about unfriending people over politics.
sentences.zh: 我打电话给萨拉，聊了聊因为政治原因而把人拉黑的事。

sentences.en: But actually, this wasn't even the main Facebook event that I'd called about.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这甚至不是我打电话谈论的主要脸书事件。

sentences.en: It was something that happened a little later in the 2016 election cycle.
sentences.zh: 那是发生在2016年大选周期稍晚时候的一件事。

sentences.en: I don't remember a specific time, but I do remember whenever it was, I told my husband, wow, my dad unfriended me.
sentences.zh: 我不记得具体是什么时候，但我确实记得无论何时，我告诉丈夫，哇，我爸把我拉黑了。

sentences.en: Sarah's dad lives near her in Colorado.
sentences.zh: 萨拉的父亲住在科罗拉多州她的住所附近。

sentences.en: He's a lifelong conservative Christian.
sentences.zh: 他是一位坚定的保守派基督徒。

sentences.en: But politics had never caused a rift between them before this.
sentences.zh: 但在此之前，政治从未在他们之间引发过裂痕。

sentences.en: She says he was an outstanding dad who she lived with exclusively as a teenager after her parents divorced.
sentences.zh: 她说他是一位杰出的父亲，父母离婚后，她青少年时期一直和他住在一起。

sentences.en: But as the 2016 presidential election ramped up, their conversations became more political.
sentences.zh: 但随着2016年总统大选的升温，他们的对话变得越来越政治化。

sentences.en: Intense.
sentences.zh: 非常激烈。

sentences.en: We were just unable to have conversations.
sentences.zh: 我们简直没法好好对话。

sentences.en: Every conversation he had had to be about politics.
sentences.zh: 他说的每一句话都必须关于政治。

sentences.en: Would you actually, do you remember, would you say like, I don't know, dad, let's talk about something else?
sentences.zh: 你真的会——你还记得吗，你会说类似“我不知道，爸，我们聊点别的吧”这样的话吗？

sentences.en: Like what were your...
sentences.zh: 比如你的那些……

sentences.en: All the time.
sentences.zh: 经常。

sentences.en: All the time.
sentences.zh: 总是这样。

sentences.en: Did you have to be subtle about it?
sentences.zh: 你必须委婉一点吗？

sentences.en: No, I have to be very direct about it.
sentences.zh: 不，我必须非常直接。

sentences.en: Dad, I don't want to talk about this.
sentences.zh: 爸，我不想谈这个。

sentences.en: Sarah kept trying unsuccessfully to change the subject, but her dad wouldn't budge.
sentences.zh: 萨拉一直试图转移话题但没有成功，但她父亲就是不肯让步。

sentences.en: And then finally, in 2016, he pulled away from Sarah.
sentences.zh: 最后，在2016年，他开始疏远萨拉。

sentences.en: First, it was the Facebook unfriending.
sentences.zh: 首先，是在脸书上取消好友。

sentences.en: And then fewer and fewer phone calls.
sentences.zh: 然后电话也越来越少。

sentences.en: We used to talk at least one or two times a week before.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，我们每周至少通一两次话。

sentences.en: And then it got to the point where we talked maybe once a month.
sentences.zh: 后来发展到我们大概一个月才通一次话。

sentences.en: And so that switch of having him being very present in my life to not being present almost at all was really devastating.
sentences.zh: 所以，从他极度融入我的生活到几乎完全消失，这种转变真的令人痛心。

sentences.en: The situation was a shock to Sarah, but it was a scenario cropping up more and more for psychologist Joshua Coleman.
sentences.zh: 这种情况对萨拉来说是个打击，但对于心理学家约书亚·科尔曼来说，这样的情景正越来越多地出现。

sentences.en: I wrote my first book on estrangement in 2007, and I don't recall working with families who'd been estranged over politics, but now it's not uncommon at all.
sentences.zh: 我在2007年写了第一本关于疏离的书，我不记得曾与因政治原因而疏远的家庭合作过，但现在这已经非常普遍了。

sentences.en: Coleman is the author of the book Rules of Estrangement.
sentences.zh: 科尔曼是《疏离规则》一书的作者。

sentences.en: He lives in the San Francisco Bay Area, and he sees a lot of clients who've been estranged by other family members.
sentences.zh: 他住在旧金山湾区，接待了许多被其他家庭成员疏远的客户。

sentences.en: But it never used to be over politics until Donald Trump first ran for president.
sentences.zh: 但以前从来不是因为政治，直到唐纳德·特朗普首次竞选总统。

sentences.en: Now, according to a survey Coleman commissioned, one in five estranged family members cite political differences as the cause.
sentences.zh: 现在，根据科尔曼委托进行的一项调查，每五个疏远的家庭成员中就有一个将政治分歧列为原因。

sentences.en: Coleman says typically it's a Trump-supporting parent being cut off by an anti-Trump child.
sentences.zh: 科尔曼说，通常是支持特朗普的父母被反特朗普的孩子断绝关系。

sentences.en: So Sarah's case is a bit different.
sentences.zh: 所以萨拉的情况有点不同。

sentences.en: But in any case, Coleman thinks there are a couple reasons for all this.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，科尔曼认为这一切背后有几个原因。

sentences.en: One is the more controversial and heated rhetoric that President Donald Trump has been charged with introducing to national politics.
sentences.zh: 一个是唐纳德·特朗普总统被指将其引入国家政治的更具争议和煽动性的言论。

sentences.en: But Coleman thinks we're to blame, too.
sentences.zh: 但科尔曼认为我们也有责任。

sentences.en: Because as a society, we seem to prize our political convictions more and more in recent decades.
sentences.zh: 因为作为一个社会，在最近的几十年里，我们似乎越来越看重我们的政治信念。

sentences.en: We're in an era where people are sort of led to believe that their identities and the preservation of their mental health are the most important North Stars to orient themselves towards.
sentences.zh: 我们处于这样一个时代：人们在某种程度上被引导去相信，他们的身份认同和心理健康的维护是他们赖以定位的最重要的北极星。

sentences.en: And it turns out that's actually not really the case.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这其实并不完全是这样。

sentences.en: The research shows that it's much more community and relationships and involvement and voluntary associations are much better North Stars for happiness and resilience and joy.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，社区、人际关系、参与以及自愿结社才是通往幸福、韧性和快乐的更好北极星。

sentences.en: I should say that the research Coleman is pointing to shows social connections are strongly linked to happiness.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，科尔曼所指的研究表明，社会联系与幸福感紧密相连。

sentences.en: It's harder to say for sure if they cause it.
sentences.zh: 很难确切地说它们是否是其诱因。

sentences.en: But either way, we know people fare better when they aren't lonely.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，我们知道人们在不感到孤独时过得更好。

sentences.en: And estrangement obviously stands in the way of that.
sentences.zh: 而家庭疏离显然阻碍了这一点。

sentences.en: Coleman is open about the fact that he tends to be against the so-called no-contact movement.
sentences.zh: 科尔曼坦言，他倾向于反对所谓的“零接触”运动。

sentences.en: It's an increasingly common trend where people, often adult children,
sentences.zh: 这是一个日益普遍的趋势，人们（通常是成年子女）

sentences.en: cut off all communication with certain family members when they experience the relationship as harmful or unmanageable.
sentences.zh: 当他们觉得这段关系有害或无法掌控时，便切断与特定家庭成员的所有联系。

sentences.en: In full transparency, by the way, Joshua Coleman was estranged from his own adult daughter for years, although not over politics, and they've since reconciled.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，坦白讲，约书亚·科尔曼本人也曾与他的成年女儿疏远多年，尽管不是因为政治原因，但他们后来已经和好了。

sentences.en: So what does he think people experiencing stress over a political disagreement with a family member should do?
sentences.zh: 那么，他认为因与家人存在政治分歧而感到压力的人应该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Well, first off...
sentences.zh: 好吧，首先……

sentences.en: It's good to be proactive, you know, before you go to that lunch or whatever.
sentences.zh: 采取积极主动的态度是好的，你知道的，在你去吃午饭或者做别的之前。

sentences.en: Say, look, you know, let's just agree we're not going to talk about Trump or politics or, you know, Israel or whatever.
sentences.zh: 说，听着，你知道的，我们只是达成一致，我们不谈论特朗普、政治，或者，你知道的，以色列什么的。

sentences.en: You know, it always goes poorly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这总是结果糟糕。

sentences.en: So can we just have that agreement?
sentences.zh: 所以我们能达成这个共识吗？

sentences.en: And the person says, no, I want to talk about what I want to talk about.
sentences.zh: 而对方说，不，我想谈我想谈的事。

sentences.en: Don't limit what I can do.
sentences.zh: 不要限制我能做的事。

sentences.en: They can say, okay, well, you can, but I just want to let you know that I won't be participating in that conversation because I don't think it's very productive.
sentences.zh: 他们可以回答，好的，好吧，你可以谈，但我只是想让你知道，我不会参与那场对话，因为我认为这没什么建设性。

sentences.en: Back in Colorado, Sarah's stalemate between her and her dad that had started around Donald Trump's win in 2016,
sentences.zh: 回到科罗拉多州，萨拉和她父亲之间始于2016年唐纳德·特朗普获胜时的僵局，

sentences.en: it extended well into 2017, Trump's first year in office.
sentences.zh: 一直持续到2017年特朗普上任的第一年。

sentences.en: It went on for seven or eight months until finally...
sentences.zh: 这种情况持续了七八个月，直到最后……

sentences.en: My husband actually called my dad and said, listen, you have one daughter and you're losing time with your daughter.
sentences.zh: 我的丈夫实际上给我爸爸打电话说，听着，你只有一个女儿，你正在失去陪伴女儿的时间。

sentences.en: You're losing time with your grandson.
sentences.zh: 你正在失去陪伴外孙的时间。

sentences.en: It's not worth it.
sentences.zh: 这不值得。

sentences.en: You need to let it go and you need to be okay with Sarah not having the same political opinions as you do.
sentences.zh: 你需要放下它，你需要接受萨拉和你没有相同的政治观点。

sentences.en: And that doesn't mean that you're any less of a person or that she's any less of a person.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你或她就是个更逊的人。

sentences.en: Do you remember what your dad said when your husband talked to him?
sentences.zh: 你还记得当你丈夫跟你爸说话时你爸说了什么吗？

sentences.en: He told him, I'll pray about it.
sentences.zh: 他对他说，我会为此祈祷的。

sentences.en: And then what?
sentences.zh: 然后呢？

sentences.en: And then I think he actually did go pray about it because he, I genuinely think he went and had a come to Jesus moment.
sentences.zh: 然后我想他真的去祈祷了，因为我真心觉得他去经历了一次醍醐灌顶的时刻。

sentences.en: I don't even say that lightly because all of a sudden it was like, I'm going to come to your house.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不是随便说说，因为突然之间就像是，我要去你家。

sentences.en: And there was more phone calls.
sentences.zh: 电话也变多了。

sentences.en: And so I was very happy to have him back.
sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴他能回来。

sentences.en: By the way, Sarah requested that I not interview her father.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，萨拉要求我不要采访她的父亲。

sentences.en: She doesn't want to cause a new rift.
sentences.zh: 她不想引发新的裂痕。

sentences.en: Sarah's husband confirmed the basic outlines of the story, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，萨拉的丈夫证实了故事的基本轮廓。

sentences.en: Sarah did want me to clarify that she is not in favor of reconciliation in all cases.
sentences.zh: 萨拉确实想让我澄清，她并不支持在所有情况下都必须和好。

sentences.en: She says if someone has a toxic or abusive relationship with a close family member, then it can be best to let go of that relationship.
sentences.zh: 她说，如果一个人与近亲的关系是有毒的或虐待性的，那么放手这段关系可能是最好的选择。

sentences.en: But that's not the relationship Sarah had with her father before all this.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是萨拉在这一切发生之前与父亲的关系。

sentences.en: Which aligns with what I heard from Joshua Coleman.
sentences.zh: 这与我从约书亚·科尔曼那里听到的一致。

sentences.en: He agrees sometimes there have to be hard boundaries.
sentences.zh: 他赞同有时候必须划定严厉的界限。

sentences.en: Like, for instance, if someone's parent kept demeaning or insulting the sexuality of their grandchild.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果某个人的父母不断贬低或侮辱他们孙辈的性取向。

sentences.en: But even then, Coleman says,
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，科尔曼说，

sentences.en: I think people deserve kind of a period of education where you're sort of saying, look, we can either agree that I know how you feel, you've already told me,
sentences.zh: 我认为人们值得拥有一段教育期，你可以这样说，听着，我们要么达成一致，我知道你的感受，你已经告诉过我了，

sentences.en: I don't need to hear it again.
sentences.zh: 我不需要再听一遍。

sentences.en: And we can either agree that we're going to have different ideas about this and you'll never speak of it again.
sentences.zh: 我们要么同意对此持有不同的看法，并且你再也不要提起它。

sentences.en: Or it makes it, it's going to make it really hard for me to want to spend time with you.
sentences.zh: 否则这会让我很难想要花时间跟你在一起。

sentences.en: You get to decide, mom or dad, kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 妈妈或爸爸，你们自己决定吧，差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: As for Sarah and her dad, their reconciliation in 2017 was not entirely permanent.
sentences.zh: 至于萨拉和她的父亲，他们在2017年的和好并非完全永久的。

sentences.en: There have been ups and downs.
sentences.zh: 期间也有过起起落落。

sentences.en: During COVID, Sarah and her dad nearly had a falling out again over her getting the COVID vaccine while pregnant.
sentences.zh: 在新冠疫情期间，萨拉和她父亲差点又因为她在怀孕期间接种新冠疫苗而闹翻。

sentences.en: Her dad was convinced it would harm the baby, which it did not.
sentences.zh: 她父亲确信这会伤害孩子，然而并没有。

sentences.en: But overall, even though nationally politics are more divisive than ever, Sarah says she and her dad are in a good place.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，尽管全国范围内的政治分歧比以往任何时候都更加分裂，但萨拉说她和父亲的关系很好。

sentences.en: I talk to him every single day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都跟他说话。

sentences.en: You talk to him every day now?
sentences.zh: 你现在每天都跟他说话？

sentences.en: Every day.
sentences.zh: 每天。

sentences.en: I see him at least once a week.
sentences.zh: 我每周至少见他一次。

sentences.en: We usually go down there on Saturday or Sunday with our kids and spend the afternoon with him.
sentences.zh: 我们通常在周六或周日带着孩子去他那儿，陪他度过整个下午。

sentences.en: We have a very loving relationship.
sentences.zh: 我们有着非常充满爱的关系。

sentences.en: And, you know, when he does get a little heated about politics, I typically just say, dad, I don't want to talk about this.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，当他在政治问题上变得有点激进时，我通常只会说，爸，我不想谈这个。

sentences.en: Or I'll just leave my husband talking politics with him and I'll walk out of the room.
sentences.zh: 或者我会让我丈夫继续跟他谈论政治，而我则走开离开房间。

sentences.en: But we have learned how to manage our emotions and just prioritize the fact that we're a family.
sentences.zh: 但我们学会了如何控制自己的情绪，并优先考虑我们是一家人这一事实。

sentences.en: Sarah and the psychologist Joshua Coleman have a couple things in common.
sentences.zh: 萨拉和心理学家约书亚·科尔曼有一些共同点。

sentences.en: First, and Coleman confirmed this with me, they are both not fans of President Trump and his policies.
sentences.zh: 首先，科尔曼向我证实了这一点，他们都不喜欢特朗普总统及其政策。

sentences.en: But also, while it isn't always possible, they both believe in attempting to maintain your closest connections across stark political divisions.
sentences.zh: 但同时，尽管并不总是可行，他们都坚信应该努力跨越巨大的政治分歧维持最亲密的联系。

sentences.en: Because if you don't, it might not just hurt the other person.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你不这样做，受伤的可能不仅仅是对方。

sentences.en: It might hurt you just as much.
sentences.zh: 它对你的伤害可能同样巨大。

sentences.en: For Call to Mind, I'm Chris Benderev.
sentences.zh: 我是克里斯·本德雷夫，为您报道“唤醒心灵”。

sentences.en: Let's take a break.
sentences.zh: 我们休息一下。

sentences.en: And when we come back, we'll tell you about an industry that's trying to stay afloat,
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将为您讲述一个努力维持生存的行业，

sentences.en: while trade turmoil and financial strain are causing the workers to wonder if they should just give up and get out.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，贸易动荡和财务压力让工人们开始琢磨是否应该直接放弃并退出。

sentences.en: That's coming up on The Strain of Stress, a Call to Mind special report from American Public Media.
sentences.zh: 该内容即将播出，节目为《压力的压力》，这是来自美国公共传媒的“唤醒心灵”特别报道。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Strain of Stress, a special report from Call to Mind,
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《压力的压力》，这是一份来自“唤醒心灵”的特别报道，

sentences.en: American Public Media's initiative to foster new conversations about mental health.
sentences.zh: “唤醒心灵”是美国公共传媒旨在促进有关心理健康新对话的倡议。

sentences.en: I'm Angela Davis.
sentences.zh: 我是安吉拉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: My name is Andrew.
sentences.zh: 我叫安德鲁。

sentences.en: I live in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 我住在宾夕法尼亚州费城。

sentences.en: Something that stresses me out is the expenses of everyday life in America right now.
sentences.zh: 让我感到压力的一件事是目前美国日常生活开销。

sentences.en: Expenses continue to rise on what feels like a monthly basis.
sentences.zh: 感觉几乎每个月生活开销都在持续上涨。

sentences.en: It costs more to keep my car insured.
sentences.zh: 为我的汽车购买保险花费更多了。

sentences.en: It's going to cost more for rent next year.
sentences.zh: 明年房租将花费更多。

sentences.en: It costs more to get food and groceries.
sentences.zh: 购买食物和杂货花费更多了。

sentences.en: I am on an Affordable Care Act plan.
sentences.zh: 我使用的是《平价医疗法案》的医保计划。

sentences.en: I fear that my premiums will go up by hundreds of dollars monthly.
sentences.zh: 我担心我的保费每月会增加几百美元。

sentences.en: That is a major source of stress.
sentences.zh: 这是一个主要的压力来源。

sentences.en: And things that would typically bring me relief from stress in everyday life, such as streaming TV shows or movies, those leisure activities are also getting more expensive.
sentences.zh: 而那些通常能在日常生活中为我缓解压力的事物，比如播放电视节目或电影，这些休闲活动也变得越来越昂贵。

sentences.en: A way that it's impacting my mental health is that it's hard to even get relief from these everyday stressors.
sentences.zh: 它对我的心理健康产生的影响是，甚至很难从这些日常压力源中得到缓解。

sentences.en: That was Andrew.
sentences.zh: 刚才那是安德鲁。

sentences.en: He's a media producer in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 他是费城的一名媒体制作人。

sentences.en: Earlier in the hour, we heard that chronic stress, persistent and long-term pressure, is tied to serious health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 在节目早些时候，我们听说慢性压力——持续和长期的压力——与严重的健康问题息息相关。

sentences.en: Chronic stress can trigger mental health challenges and make existing mental illnesses worse.
sentences.zh: 慢性压力会引发心理健康挑战，并使现有的精神疾病恶化。

sentences.en: National surveys report one of the most common and often the primary source of stress in our lives is work.
sentences.zh: 全国调查报告称，我们生活中最常见、往往也是主要的压力来源之一是工作。

sentences.en: Whether it's hustle culture, a difficult workload, conflict among colleagues, or never being able to get ahead,
sentences.zh: 无论是内卷文化、沉重的工作负荷、同事之间的冲突，还是永远无法领先一步，

sentences.en: nearly 7 in 10 employed adults identify work-related stress as a significant burden.
sentences.zh: 近7成的受雇成年人认为工作相关压力是一个沉重的负担。

sentences.en: High on the list of work stress, a difficult or toxic workplace.
sentences.zh: 在工作压力的名单中排名靠前的是，困难或有毒的工作场所。

sentences.en: Also high on the list, job insecurity.
sentences.zh: 同样名列前茅的还有工作不稳定性。

sentences.en: A good example is the agricultural industry.
sentences.zh: 农业就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Farmers face a lot of job insecurities.
sentences.zh: 农民面临着很多工作不稳定性。

sentences.en: There's trade conflict, rising costs, climate change, and farmers bear the brunt of it all.
sentences.zh: 存在贸易冲突、成本上升、气候变化，而农民承担了这一切的首当其冲的后果。

sentences.en: Studies show that all of this leads to increased rates of stress, depression, and suicide in farm country.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，所有这一切导致了乡村地区压力、抑郁和自杀率的上升。

sentences.en: Mental health providers say some farmers seek help, but they also say our health care system needs to rethink how care is delivered to farmers.
sentences.zh: 心理健康提供者表示，一些农民寻求帮助，但他们也表示我们的医疗保健系统需要重新思考如何向农民提供护理。

sentences.en: Minnesota Public Radio's Molly Castle Work and Tadeo Ruiz-Sandoval have more.
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达公共广播电台的莫莉·卡斯特·沃克和塔代奥·鲁伊斯·桑多瓦尔为您带来更多报道。
zh_words: 塔代奥·鲁伊斯·桑多瓦尔

sentences.en: It's a chilly November day in north-central Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 这里是美国明尼苏达州中北部，一个阴冷的11月天。

sentences.en: Dave Gary, a soybean and corn farmer, is driving his truck heading home.
sentences.zh: 大豆和玉米种植农场主戴夫·加里正开着卡车回家。

sentences.en: He just dropped off some of his corn harvest at a grain elevator in the town of Warren.
sentences.zh: 他刚刚把一部分玉米收成卸在沃伦镇的一个谷物升降机仓库里。

sentences.en: This is where most farmers in the area sell their crops.
sentences.zh: 当地大多数农场主都是在这里出售他们的农作物。

sentences.en: Dave expects his corn to sell at a loss due to ongoing international trade turmoil that is hitting corn prices hard.
sentences.zh: 戴夫预计由于持续的国际贸易动荡严重打击了玉米价格，他的玉米卖出去会亏本。

sentences.en: It's a situation that's made the local grain elevator feel to Gary less like a place of commerce and more like a casino.
sentences.zh: 这种情况让加里觉得当地的谷物仓库与其说是一个商业场所，不如说更像是一个赌场。

sentences.en: It's a crapshoot.
sentences.zh: 这完全是个碰运气的事。

sentences.en: It's a roll of the dice.
sentences.zh: 这就好比掷骰子。

sentences.en: Two years ago, Dave Gary almost went bankrupt after a business he contracted with to sell his crop of sunflower seeds went buSt.
sentences.zh: 两年前，戴夫·加里差点破产，因为他签约销售向日葵种子的那家公司倒闭了。

sentences.en: We couldn't pay our bills and it about took us out of farming.
sentences.zh: 我们连账单都付不起，差点就做不成农民了。

sentences.en: It really did.
sentences.zh: 真的差点就做不成了。

sentences.en: If it wasn't for our family, we probably would have been done farming.
sentences.zh: 要不是有家人支持，我们可能早就放弃务农了。

sentences.en: If farming was ever once a simple life, it no longer is.
sentences.zh: 如果农业曾经算是一种简单的小日子，那它现在已经不是了。

sentences.en: Today, more farmers are piling up high levels of debt and filing for bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 如今，越来越多的农民背负着高额债务并申请破产。

sentences.en: The average age of farmers continues to skew older and few young people are interested in continuing farm work.
sentences.zh: 农民的平均年龄持续老化，几乎没有什么年轻人对继续从事农业感兴趣。

sentences.en: Dave says this has stressed both him and his wife.
sentences.zh: 戴夫说这给他和妻子都带来了巨大的压力。

sentences.en: She's like, why do you want to keep doing this?
sentences.zh: 她总是问：你为什么还要继续干这个？

sentences.en: Well, it's in my blood.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是刻在我骨子里的。

sentences.en: I don't know what else to do.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道除了这个还能做什么。

sentences.en: Dave Gary's family arrived to the United States in the 1900s via ship from Ireland.
sentences.zh: 戴夫·加里的家族在20世纪初坐着从爱尔兰出发的轮船来到了美国。

sentences.en: His grandparents survived the Great Depression, while his parents weathered the 1980s farm crisis.
sentences.zh: 他的祖父母在大萧条中幸存了下来，而他的父母则熬过了20世纪80年代的农业危机。

sentences.en: So there's a little legacy there.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面也有一些家族传承。

sentences.en: And I don't want to be the generation that loses the family farm.
sentences.zh: 我可不想成为丢掉家族农场的那一代人。

sentences.en: But it's getting tougher and tougher to hold on every year.
sentences.zh: 但要坚持下去，一年比一年难了。

sentences.en: Gary is like many American farmers today, feeling isolated, unprofitable, and putting huge amounts of pressure on themselves to keep the farm going.
sentences.zh: 加里就像如今许多美国农民一样，感到孤立无援、无利可图，并承受着维持农场运转的巨大心理压力。

sentences.en: Tracy Rutherford Self is an agricultural mental health specialist for the state of Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 特雷西·卢瑟福·塞尔夫是明尼苏达州的农业心理健康专家。

sentences.en: She says the mental health landscape for farmers across the country is unsettling.
sentences.zh: 她说，全国各地农民的心理健康状况令人担忧。

sentences.en: I always ask people about suicide.
sentences.zh: 我总是会问人们关于自杀的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, when I'm working with farmers, it's going to be one of my first questions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我与农民交错时，这往往是我最先提出的问题之一。

sentences.en: Farming is one of the industries with the highest risk for suicide.
sentences.zh: 农业是自杀风险最高的行业之一。

sentences.en: A common thread?
sentences.zh: 一个共同的线索是什么？

sentences.en: Finances especially are taking their toll.
sentences.zh: 尤其是财务问题正在造成沉重的打击。

sentences.en: Purdue University reported that nationally, farmers are feeling more pessimistic about the future of U.S.
sentences.zh: 普渡大学报告称，从全国来看，农民对美国农业的未来感到更加悲观。

sentences.en: agriculture.
sentences.zh: 农业。

sentences.en: The feeling rose sharply at the start of 2026 amid growing economic concerns.
sentences.zh: 在经济担忧加剧的背景下，这种情绪在2026年初急剧上升。

sentences.en: And Rutherford Self says finances have been extra unpredictable lately with the rapidly changing federal tariff policies.
sentences.zh: 卢瑟福·塞尔夫表示，由于联邦关税政策瞬息万变，最近财务状况变得格外难以预测。

sentences.en: Right now, for many farmers, things change, again, almost daily, where markets will swing because of things that are happening at the government level.
sentences.zh: 眼下，对许多农民来说，情况几乎每天都在变，市场会因为政府层面的事情而剧烈波动。

sentences.en: The amount of things that you can control in the year are shrinking and shrinking.
sentences.zh: 这一年里你能掌控的事情越来越少。

sentences.en: That's Kahler Rosanaw, a corn and soybean farmer who lives in northeast North Dakota.
sentences.zh: 那是卡勒·罗萨诺，一位住在北达科他州东北部的玉米和大豆农场主。

sentences.en: Kahler became a full-time farmer two years before the U.S.
sentences.zh: 卡勒在美国对中国这个美国主要贸易伙伴发动贸易战的两年前，成为了一名全职农民。

sentences.en: entered the trade war with China, a major American trade partner.
sentences.zh: 进入贸易战，这是个主要的美国贸易伙伴。

sentences.en: That caused Rosanaw to bleed money.
sentences.zh: 这导致罗萨诺血本无归。

sentences.en: It just came all together to a point where you just didn't feel like you had control of anything.
sentences.zh: 这一切汇聚到了一起，让你觉得你对任何事情都失去了控制。

sentences.en: And it was very frustrating.
sentences.zh: 这让人感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: Government subsidies helped Kahler stay afloat.
sentences.zh: 政府的补贴帮助卡勒勉强维持了生计。

sentences.en: Barely.
sentences.zh: 勉强维持。

sentences.en: Now, amidst the second agricultural trade war, Rosanaw's wallet is once again under strain.
sentences.zh: 如今，在第二次农业贸易战中，罗萨诺的钱包再次承受着压力。

sentences.en: And once more, he's expecting government farm subsidies to help some, but not enough.
sentences.zh: 而且这一次，他预计政府的农业补贴能起一点作用，但远远不够。

sentences.en: How many years can we keep doing this?
sentences.zh: 我们还能这样坚持几年？

sentences.en: How many years are we going to have the social capital of the American taxpayer to keep bailing out the American farmer?
sentences.zh: 美国纳税人的社会资本还要花多少年去不断接济美国农民？

sentences.en: Which, we don't want the payments, we just want the price of the market.
sentences.zh: 其实，我们并不想要这种救济金，我们只想要正常的价格。

sentences.en: Who do you talk to about this?
sentences.zh: 你这种事能跟谁说呢？

sentences.en: It's got to go somewhere, right?
sentences.zh: 总得有个倾诉的出口吧？

sentences.en: Like, I can't imagine it's healthy or easy to just keep it in.
sentences.zh: 我觉得把事情全憋在心里肯定既不健康也不容易。

sentences.en: Well, I've got a lot of farmer friends, and we're all in the same boat, talking to them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有很多农民朋友，我们都处境相同，会跟他们聊聊。

sentences.en: They share, they're in the same situation you are, talking to them, talking it over, seeing what they're going to do.
sentences.zh: 他们会分享，他们经历的状况和你一样，和他们聊聊，商量一下，看看他们打算怎么做。

sentences.en: It gives you kind of some reassurances that you're not the only one going through this.
sentences.zh: 这能给你一种安慰，让你觉得经历这些的不止你一个人。

sentences.en: Farmers in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国的农民向来以坚忍著称。

sentences.en: have a reputation for stoicism.
sentences.zh: 拥有坚忍的声誉。

sentences.en: So when therapy is based on talk, it can be hard to get them to come in and speak with a stranger about their probleMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，当心理治疗主要靠交谈时，很难让他们主动走进来跟陌生人倾诉他们的烦恼。

sentences.en: It's just very difficult for farmers to ask for help.
sentences.zh: 农民要开口寻求帮助实在是太难了。

sentences.en: You know, they're very independent, so I think they just really try to solve their own probleMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们非常独立，所以我认为他们真的在极力自己解决问题。

sentences.en: That's Cynthia Christensen, a therapist in Minnesota who has counseled farmers for 18 years.
sentences.zh: 那是辛西娅·克里斯滕森，明尼苏达州的一名治疗师，她为农民提供心理咨询已有18年。

sentences.en: Christensen grew up on an Iowa cattle farm and says she understands how farmers can feel judged for admitting that they're struggling.
sentences.zh: 克里斯滕森在爱荷华州的一个养牛场长大，她说她理解农民在承认自己苦苦挣扎时为什么会感到被人评判。

sentences.en: There's a lot of stigma attached to seeking a therapist in the rural environment.
sentences.zh: 在农村环境中，寻求心理治疗伴随着巨大的污名化。

sentences.en: I wish I wasn't saying that, but I think it's, I feel like people, it takes a lot of courage for somebody to call me.
sentences.zh: 我真希望我不用这么说，但我觉得，人们需要很大的勇气才能给我打电话。

sentences.en: So, if mental health professionals want to help more farmers, Christensen and her colleague Tracy Rutherford Self say the industry needs to rethink how their services are provided.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果心理健康专业人士想要帮助更多的农民，克里斯滕森和她的同事特雷西·卢瑟福·塞尔夫表示，该行业需要重新思考其服务提供方式。

sentences.en: For example, Rutherford Self visits her clients on the farm or neutral spots like community college campuses.
sentences.zh: 例如，卢瑟福·塞尔夫会直接去农场拜访客户，或者约在社区学院校园等中立地点。

sentences.en: They don't want to be seen coming into an office, and that's not even stigma.
sentences.zh: 他们不想被人看到自己走进办公室，这甚至还不是因为什么污名化。

sentences.en: But there's some reality to, hey, if somebody sees me going into a therapy office, what are they going to think about me?
sentences.zh: 但这里面有一个现实问题，那就是：嘿，如果有人看到我走进心理诊所，他们会怎么看我？

sentences.en: And what they think about me literally could impact my livelihood.
sentences.zh: 而他们的看法实际上可能会影响到我的生计。

sentences.en: Rutherford Self says if the local banker knows a farmer is struggling, it might be harder for that client to get a loan for seed or a new tractor.
sentences.zh: 卢瑟福·塞尔夫说，如果当地的银行家知道某个农民正在苦苦挣扎，那这位客户想申请购买种子或新拖拉机的贷款可能会更难。

sentences.en: And if mental health providers want to build trust with their clients, they need to show that they understand the unique pressures of farming.
sentences.zh: 如果心理健康服务提供商想要与客户建立信任，他们就需要表明自己理解农业特有的压力。

sentences.en: Rutherford Self says she explains early on in sessions about her own rural upbringing and that her husband comes from a farm family.
sentences.zh: 卢瑟福·塞尔夫说，她在咨询刚开始时就会向客户解释自己的农村成长背景，并说明她丈夫也来自一个农民家庭。

sentences.en: If farmers do come in for a therapy session, out-of-touch comments can discourage them from returning.
sentences.zh: 如果农民真的来做心理咨询，一些不接地气的言论可能会打消他们再次前来的念头。

sentences.en: I had a client who recently told me they went to see a provider, and at the end of the session, the provider told them that they would just be better off not farming.
sentences.zh: 我曾有一个客户最近告诉我，他们去看了一位心理医生，结果在咨询结束时，医生告诉他们，如果不干农活可能会过得更好。

sentences.en: And while on some level there actually may be some truth to that as far as finances and stress, I think it really shows a lack of understanding of what our farmers really value,
sentences.zh: 虽然在某种程度上，就财务和压力而言，这可能确实有些道理，但我认为这真正反映出他们缺乏对我们农民真正珍视之物的理解，

sentences.en: and that is legacy and being able to continue to do the work.
sentences.zh: 那就是家族传承以及能够继续从事这项工作的能力。

sentences.en: Tracy Rutherford Self says not only do communities need to train more providers to work in rural areas,
sentences.zh: 特雷西·卢瑟福·塞尔夫说，不仅社区需要培训更多人在农村地区开展工作，

sentences.en: but the mental health care system also needs to think more expansively about who can help.
sentences.zh: 而且心理健康保健系统也需要更广泛地思考究竟谁能提供帮助。

sentences.en: I have a really big philosophy that if you wait for the first call to come straight to me, we're going to miss people.
sentences.zh: 我有一个非常坚定的理念，那就是如果你只是坐等第一个求助电话直接打给我，我们就会漏掉很多人。

sentences.en: When people are struggling, especially farmers, their first call isn't to a therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 当人们陷入困境时，尤其是农民，他们打出的第一个电话通常不是给治疗师的。

sentences.en: It's to family, a friend.
sentences.zh: 而是打给家人或朋友。

sentences.en: Rutherford Self says mental health providers should leverage this, training all kinds of community members to recognize mental health warning signs.
sentences.zh: 卢瑟福·塞尔夫说，心理健康服务提供者应该善加利用这一点，培训各种社区成员来识别心理健康预警信号。

sentences.en: She's training some bankers right now because they're often the first to hear if a farmer is struggling financially.
sentences.zh: 她目前正在培训一些银行职员，因为他们往往最先听到农民陷入财务困境的消息。

sentences.en: Christensen suggests that more everyday people in rural communities should get trained to recognize and watch for the signs of mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 克里斯滕森建议，农村社区的更多普通人应当接受培训，以便识别并关注心理健康问题的迹象。

sentences.en: In rural communities, you know, because of the population numbers, you know, we all have to kind of know some CPR, something about the Heimlich Maneuver,
sentences.zh: 在农村社区，你知道，由于人口数量的原因，我们大家都必须懂得一些心肺复苏术，或者海姆立克急救法之类的知识，

sentences.en: and I think it's the same kind of life-saving thing that we know something about the questions that we can ask to see if our neighbors are struggling with their mental health.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是一种救命的技能，我们需要了解可以向邻居提出哪些问题，来看看他们是否正遭受心理健康问题的困扰。

sentences.en: The farmers we met for this story, Dave Gehry and Kayla Rosenau, both say they're not planning to seek mental health support right now.
sentences.zh: 我们在这次报道中遇到的两位农民，戴夫·加里和卡勒·罗萨诺都表示，他们目前并不打算寻求心理健康支持。

sentences.en: Dave laughs, actually, when I ask him about the hardships.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我问起这些艰难困苦时，戴夫笑了。

sentences.en: He says he's going to rely on his friends, and they, in turn, rely on him.
sentences.zh: 他说他会依靠他的朋友们，而他的朋友们反过来也会依靠他。

sentences.en: I get a lot of calls from friends and neighbors that are having tough days, and they don't want to take it home with them, so they end up calling you,
sentences.zh: 我经常接到朋友和邻居的电话，他们遇到了艰难的一天，又不想把负面情绪带回家里，所以最后只好打电话给你，

sentences.en: and you talk them off the ledge.
sentences.zh: 然后你帮他们走出绝境。

sentences.en: But mental health experts say Dave Gehry's approach isn't sustainable for everyone.
sentences.zh: 但心理健康专家表示，戴夫·加里这种方法并非对每个人都可持续。

sentences.en: They say the mental health system across the country needs to adapt so that farmers like Dave Gehry trust that when they are struggling or stressed, they can come in and get help.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，全国各地的心理健康系统需要进行调整，以便像戴夫·加里这样的农民在感到挣扎或压力时，能够相信他们可以进来寻求帮助。

sentences.en: For Call to Mind, I'm Molly Castlework.
sentences.zh: 我是莫莉·卡斯特沃克，为您报道《心随灵动》。

sentences.en: And I'm Tadeo Ruiz-Sandoval in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 我是塔德奥·鲁伊斯·桑多瓦尔，在明尼苏达州为您报道。
zh_words: 塔德奥·鲁伊斯·桑多瓦尔

sentences.en: You're listening to The Strain of Stress, a special report from Call to Mind.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《压力的重担》，这是《心随灵动》的一期特别报道。

sentences.en: I'm Angela Davis.
sentences.zh: 我是安吉拉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: At this point in the hour, it should be clear that ongoing stress is bad for us.
sentences.zh: 听到这里，大家应该已经清楚，持续的压力对我们有害无益。

sentences.en: Not only does it change our mood, but it can damage our health and well-being.
sentences.zh: 它不仅会改变我们的情绪，还会损害我们的健康和福祉。

sentences.en: Psychologist Alyssa Eppel at the University of California, San Francisco, is an international expert on stress.
sentences.zh: 加州大学旧金山分校的心理学家阿莉莎·埃佩尔是研究压力的国际专家。

sentences.en: Alyssa has contributed groundbreaking research on how stress changes the brain and can even accelerate aging.
sentences.zh: 阿莉莎在压力如何改变大脑甚至加速衰老方面做出了突破性的研究贡献。

sentences.en: Here's Dr. Eppel.
sentences.zh: 下面请听埃佩尔博士的讲解。

sentences.en: We know from many studies now that chronic stress actually changes the structure of the brain.
sentences.zh: 我们从现有的许多研究中了解到，长期压力实际上会改变大脑的结构。

sentences.en: It can shrink parts of the brain, like the hippocampus, which is so sensitive for memory and emotion processing.
sentences.zh: 它会使大脑的某些部分萎缩，比如海马体，它对记忆和情绪处理极为敏感。

sentences.en: It can enlarge the amygdala, which, again, makes us more sensitive to threat.
sentences.zh: 它会使杏仁核变大，这同样会让我们对威胁更加敏感。

sentences.en: And it can damage or impair our prefrontal cortex, our ability to really regulate stress and problem-solve.
sentences.zh: 它还会损害或削弱我们的前额叶皮层，从而影响我们调节压力和解决问题的能力。

sentences.en: Can you give me an example of how chronic stress could change a person's cognition or how it would change the brain?
sentences.zh: 你能举个例子说明长期压力如何改变一个人的认知或大脑吗？

sentences.en: It creates cognition that's much more narrowly focused on looking for stress and danger in our environment.
sentences.zh: 它产生的认知会更加狭隘地专注于寻找我们环境中的压力和危险。

sentences.en: And so instead of seeing beauty or noticing what's right, it's the opposite.
sentences.zh: 所以，与其去发现美或注意到正确的事，结果恰恰相反。

sentences.en: So it's like focusing on what could go wrong rather than being present in the moment and appreciating what is there in front of you and what is good?
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是专注于可能会出错的事情，而不是活在当下、去感激眼前拥有的一切以及美好的事物？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: When we're stressed, our bodies release cortisol to stay alert.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到压力时，我们的身体会释放皮质醇以保持警觉。

sentences.en: And cortisol signals glucose, which is sugar, that gives us a boost of energy during stressful times.
sentences.zh: 皮质醇会向葡萄糖（也就是糖分）发出信号，在压力时期为我们提供能量补充。

sentences.en: So when cortisol is constantly triggering glucose and other hormones that activate during stress, that's when problems can show up in our bodies.
sentences.zh: 因此，当皮质醇不断触发葡萄糖以及在压力下激活的其他激素时，我们的身体就会出现问题。

sentences.en: Our blood pressure can change, our metabolism might slow down, and even our bones can get weaker.
sentences.zh: 我们的血压可能会发生变化，新陈代谢可能会减慢，甚至我们的骨骼也会变弱。

sentences.en: Dr. Alyssa Eppel says some people gain weight or develop belly fat.
sentences.zh: 阿莉莎·埃佩尔博士表示，有些人会体重增加或长出腹部脂肪。

sentences.en: But there are other clues, changes in our well-being to look for if the flood of cortisol becomes a problem.
sentences.zh: 但如果皮质醇泛滥成为一个问题，还有其他一些迹象和福祉的变化需要我们去注意。

sentences.en: When we feel that we are not able to sleep well due to stress,
sentences.zh: 当我们觉得由于压力而无法好好入睡时，

sentences.en: that is one of the biggest signs that we better pay attention and make some changes to manage our daily stress response.
sentences.zh: 这就是最显著的信号之一，说明我们最好引起重视并做出一些改变来管理日常的压力反应。

sentences.en: When we are feeling particularly irritable, when our appetite becomes untied to mealtimes and we just feel hungry all the time, when we feel lack of appetite,
sentences.zh: 当我们感到格外易怒，当我们的食欲与进餐时间脱节、感觉自己总是饿，或者当我们感到食欲不振时，

sentences.en: those are often signs we are under chronic stress.
sentences.zh: 这些往往都是我们正承受长期压力的信号。

sentences.en: I think we've all felt that our stress can age us, but your research has found it actually does.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都曾感觉到压力会使我们衰老，但你们的研究发现它确实如此。

sentences.en: How does stress age a person?
sentences.zh: 压力是如何使人衰老的？

sentences.en: When we have a stress response that's prolonged and we don't get recovery, we know that the cellular aging processes are impaired and accelerated.
sentences.zh: 当我们产生持久的压力反应且无法恢复时，我们知道细胞衰老过程会受损并加速。

sentences.en: So for example, when we have chronic stress for years and years, we tend to develop inflammation.
sentences.zh: 例如，当我们承受经年累月的长期压力时，我们往往会出现炎症。

sentences.en: We tend to develop shorter telomeres.
sentences.zh: 我们的端粒往往会变短。

sentences.en: That means our cells can't go on and keep replicating and dividing and replenishing tissue.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们的细胞无法继续复制、分裂和补充组织。

sentences.en: We also are changing our epigenetic patterns.
sentences.zh: 我们还在改变我们的表观遗传模式。

sentences.en: And so we now know that we can measure how old our cells are and that chronic stress accelerates our epigenetic age.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在知道，我们可以测量细胞的年龄，而长期压力会加速我们的表观遗传年龄。

sentences.en: The term Dr. Eppel just used, epigenetic age, is a measure of a person's biological age, not the calendar.
sentences.zh: 埃佩尔博士刚刚使用的“表观遗传年龄”这个词，是衡量一个人生物学年龄的标准，而不是按日历计算的年龄。

sentences.en: Instead of counting the years a person has been alive, epigenetic age reflects how fast our cells are aging due to our genetics, lifestyle, environment, and stress.
sentences.zh: 表观遗传年龄不计算一个人活了多少年，而是反映我们的细胞由于遗传、生活方式、环境和压力而老化的速度。

sentences.en: All of our organs are vulnerable to the effects of chronic stress.
sentences.zh: 我们所有的器官都容易受到长期压力影响的侵害。

sentences.en: The common pathway is the immune system.
sentences.zh: 共同的途径是免疫系统。

sentences.en: Stress causes premature aging of the immune system.
sentences.zh: 压力会导致免疫系统过早老化。

sentences.en: And of course, that is the fuel source and the life source for every cell in our bodies.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是我们体内每个细胞的能量源泉和生命之源。

sentences.en: Are people who have many beautiful high-stress moments like the winning athletes or business owners who love their jobs, but they have a lot of stress to keep it going,
sentences.zh: 那些经历过很多精彩高压时刻的人，比如获胜的运动员或热爱自己工作但为了维持现状而承受巨大压力的企业主，

sentences.en: can that good stress, can that accelerate aging?
sentences.zh: 这种好压力会加速衰老吗？

sentences.en: In general, no, they don't.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，不会，它们不会。

sentences.en: Because our body is exquisitely adapted to recover from those peaks of stress arousal.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的身体已经完美地适应了从那些压力激增的峰值中恢复过来。

sentences.en: The hard part is that we really need to be honest with ourselves and ask, is this good stress or is this too much?
sentences.zh: 困难的部分在于，我们需要对自己诚实，并问问自己：这是好压力，还是压力过大了？

sentences.en: Too much of a good thing, in a sense.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是物极必反。

sentences.en: That's Dr. Alyssa Eppel from the University of California, San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 以上是来自加州大学旧金山分校的阿莉莎·埃佩尔博士。

sentences.en: We'll hear from her again later.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们将继续听取她的分享。

sentences.en: You're listening to The Strain of Stress, a special report from Call to Mind.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《压力的重担》，这是《心随灵动》的一期特别报道。

sentences.en: I'm Angela Davis.
sentences.zh: 我是安吉拉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: I'm Angela Davis.
sentences.zh: 我是安吉拉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: They feel joy.
sentences.zh: 他们感受到了快乐。

sentences.en: But as we just heard from Dr. Alyssa Eppel, an important question to ask is, when is stress, even the good kind, just too much?
sentences.zh: 但正如我们刚刚从阿莉莎·埃佩尔博士那里听到的那样，我们需要提出的一个重要问题是：压力（甚至是那种好的压力）在什么时候就会变得过头了？

sentences.en: Call to Mind's Jessica Bari takes us to a big city hospital.
sentences.zh: Call to Mind 的杰西卡·巴里带我们走进一家大城市医院。

sentences.en: May we have EDS?
sentences.zh: 我们可以用急诊分诊系统吗？

sentences.en: And really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: For triage, please.
sentences.zh: 请用于分诊。

sentences.en: EDS, for triage.
sentences.zh: 急诊分诊系统，用于分诊。

sentences.en: And thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: This is the emergency department at Rush University Medical Center in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 这里是芝加哥拉什大学医学中心的急诊室。

sentences.en: It looks similar to a hospital you might see on a nighttime TV show.
sentences.zh: 它看起来和你在夜间电视节目中看到的医院差不多。

sentences.en: Staff in scrubs and white coats are quickly moving in and out of their workstations.
sentences.zh: 身穿手术服和白大褂的工作人员在工作台之间快速进出。

sentences.en: There are constant beeps and ringing noises.
sentences.zh: 各种蜂鸣声和铃声此起彼伏。

sentences.en: I'm here to meet...
sentences.zh: 我来这里是想见……

sentences.en: Corey Goldstein, and I am an attending physician in the emergency department.
sentences.zh: 科里·戈尔茨坦，我是急诊室的主治医师。

sentences.en: Dr. Corey Goldstein is supervising the shift tonight.
sentences.zh: 科里·戈尔茨坦医生今晚负责带班。

sentences.en: He's in his 50s and has practiced emergency medicine for almost a decade.
sentences.zh: 他五十多岁，从事急诊医学工作近十年。

sentences.en: The first thing Dr. Goldstein does to start his hospital shift is a sign-off meeting with the morning team.
sentences.zh: 戈尔茨坦医生开始值班时做的第一件事，就是与早班团队进行交接会议。

sentences.en: They cycle through their cases.
sentences.zh: 他们逐一过病例。

sentences.en: All right, next one.
sentences.zh: 好的，下一个。

sentences.en: Female in her 30s.
sentences.zh: 30多岁女性。

sentences.en: History of basically anxiety on coferenolol.
sentences.zh: 基本上有服用卡维地洛的焦虑症病史。

sentences.en: Coming in with bilateral lingual...
sentences.zh: 因双侧舌部……前来就诊。

sentences.en: 68-year-old male.
sentences.zh: 68岁男性。

sentences.en: Presenter AD with abdominal pain, history of diabetes, and hypertension.
sentences.zh: 汇报人AD，有腹痛症状，既往有糖尿病和高血压病史。

sentences.en: He was very tender to the right...
sentences.zh: 他对右侧……非常压痛。

sentences.en: Mid-40s male.
sentences.zh: 40岁左右男性。

sentences.en: There are about 90 patients in the emergency department and another 20 people waiting in the lobby.
sentences.zh: 急诊室里大约有90名患者，大厅里还有另外20人在等待。

sentences.en: The unit is busy.
sentences.zh: 这个科室很忙碌。

sentences.en: Rush University Medical Center is a level 2 trauma hospital.
sentences.zh: 拉什大学医学中心是一家二级创伤医院。

sentences.en: That means the staff typically doesn't treat gunshot injuries or survivors of bad car accidents.
sentences.zh: 这意味着医护人员通常不治疗枪伤或严重车祸幸存者。

sentences.en: But any shift could involve heart attacks, overdose cases, bad allergic reactions, stroke symptoms, and all manner of illness.
sentences.zh: 但任何一个班次都可能涉及心脏病发作、药物过量、严重过敏反应、中风症状以及各种各样的疾病。

sentences.en: There is no way of knowing what will happen each shift, which in itself seems stressful.
sentences.zh: 你无法预知每个班次会发生什么，这本身就让人觉得压力很大。

sentences.en: Once the sign-off meeting is finished, Dr. Goldstein starts making rounds.
sentences.zh: 交接会议结束后，戈尔茨坦医生开始查房。

sentences.en: So the patient I'm going to go see has multiple medical issues, including a organ transplant.
sentences.zh: 我要去看的这位病人有多种内科问题，包括做过器官移植。

sentences.en: I tag along, but I don't go into any examinations to respect people's privacy.
sentences.zh: 我随行参观，但为了尊重患者隐私，我不会进入任何检查室。

sentences.en: Dr. Goldstein says this is a complicated case, and the person will probably be admitted to the hospital for a few days.
sentences.zh: 戈尔茨坦医生说这是一个复杂的病例，这位患者可能需要在医院住几天。

sentences.en: Dr. Corey Goldstein moves to the next patient, and the next and the next.
sentences.zh: 科里·戈尔茨坦医生走向下一个病人，接着是一个又一个。

sentences.en: Over the course of an 8-hour shift, he rarely quits moving or takes breaks.
sentences.zh: 在长达8小时的值班过程中，他几乎从未停止走动或休息。

sentences.en: Considering the fast pace, the high volume of patients, the constant noise and beeping, and the often high-stakes decision-making, this is a stressful job.
sentences.zh: 考虑到快节奏、大量的患者、持续的噪音和蜂鸣声，以及往往高风险的决策，这是一份压力很大的工作。

sentences.en: To understand how people work in such tense environments, I talked to psychologist Dennis Stolle.
sentences.zh: 为了解人们如何在如此紧张的环境中工作，我采访了心理学家丹尼斯·施托尔。

sentences.en: He's the head of applied psychology at the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 他是美国心理协会的应用心理学负责人。

sentences.en: Much of his research is focused on the workplace, human performance, and leadership.
sentences.zh: 他的许多研究都集中在职场、人类表现和领导力上。

sentences.en: Dennis Stolle says every job involves some amount of stress, and that's not necessarily a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 丹尼斯·施托尔表示，每项工作都伴随着一定程度的压力，这不一定是件坏事。

sentences.en: That stress in the right dose is part of what helps us get out of bed in the morning, because we're concerned about the consequences of not getting those things done.
sentences.zh: 适度的压力正是帮助我们早晨起床的原因之一，因为我们担心完不成这些事情的后果。

sentences.en: And so, generally speaking, stress is not a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，总的来说，压力并不是坏事。

sentences.en: It's just part of life.
sentences.zh: 它只是生活的一部分。

sentences.en: It only becomes a bad thing when it starts to become unmanaged.
sentences.zh: 只有当压力开始失控时，它才会变成坏事。

sentences.en: Well, the number of patients in the emergency department stresses me out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，急诊室里病人的数量让我感到压力山大。

sentences.en: And I have to imagine it's overwhelming for the staff at times, too.
sentences.zh: 我想这对工作人员来说有时也是一种压倒性的负担。

sentences.en: But when I asked Dr. Corey Goldstein about it, he was matter-of-fact.
sentences.zh: 但当我向科里·戈尔茨坦医生问起这件事时，他的态度很务实。

sentences.en: Yeah, we are taking care of a lot of people simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 对，我们同时在照顾很多人。

sentences.en: But, you know, when you do anything, a lot, you get used to it, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当你经常做某件事时，你就会习惯它，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Psychologist Dennis Stolle of the American Psychological Association says high-functioning teams in stressful work environments like this
sentences.zh: 美国心理协会的心理学家丹尼斯·施托尔表示，像这样压力重重的职场环境中，高效的团队

sentences.en: typically have good communication and strong psychological safety.
sentences.zh: 通常具备良好的沟通和强大的心理安全感。

sentences.en: Here's what he means by that.
sentences.zh: 这就是他所表达的意思。

sentences.en: People feel safe to speak up and ask questions, to admit mistakes, without a fear that they're going to be punished or embarrassed for doing so.
sentences.zh: 人们感到可以安全地发表意见、提出问题、承认错误，而不必担心因此受到惩罚或尴尬。

sentences.en: And it's that kind of communication that can really be effective and let people work together in a productive kind of way.
sentences.zh: 正是这种沟通才能真正发挥作用，让人们以富有成效的方式合作。

sentences.en: It can become very unproductive if people feel a fear of speaking up.
sentences.zh: 如果人们害怕开口说话，工作就会变得非常低效。

sentences.en: I definitely saw moments when the emergency department staff seemed to have strong psychological safety.
sentences.zh: 我确实看到了急诊室员工似乎拥有强大心理安全感的时刻。

sentences.en: Like when a resident named Tim was briefing Dr. Corey Goldstein about a case.
sentences.zh: 比如有个叫蒂姆的住院医师向科里·戈尔茨坦医生汇报病例时。

sentences.en: Did you go to the dime room?
sentences.zh: 你去过那个小房间了吗？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我去过了。

sentences.en: And I'll tell you why.
sentences.zh: 我会告诉你原因。

sentences.en: Okay, tell me.
sentences.zh: 好的，告诉我。

sentences.en: He's coming over to this.
sentences.zh: 他正朝这边走来。

sentences.en: He has to came a lot of rest today.
sentences.zh: 他今天必须……

sentences.en: He described this as part of the association of lightheadedness.
sentences.zh: 他把这描述为头晕症状的一部分。

sentences.en: It's like a rope spitting.
sentences.zh: 就像……

sentences.en: Everyone on the emergency department team seemed sharp.
sentences.zh: 急诊室团队里的每个人看起来都很精干。

sentences.en: Roles were well-defined.
sentences.zh: 职责分工明确。

sentences.en: And Dr. Corey Goldstein was calmly in charge.
sentences.zh: 科里·戈尔茨坦医生冷静地掌控着全局。

sentences.en: I asked psychologist Dennis Stolle how much strong leadership factors into workplace stress levels.
sentences.zh: 我问心理学家丹尼斯·施托尔，强大的领导力在职场压力水平中占有多大的影响因素。

sentences.en: For a highly skilled, more junior worker, a critical resource to have is a highly skilled leader.
sentences.zh: 对于一个技能高超、资历较浅的员工来说，拥有一位高水平的领导是一项至关重要的资源。

sentences.en: And that reduces your stress level tremendously because you know you've got that person there who you can count on.
sentences.zh: 这会极大地降低你的压力水平，因为你知道身边有这样一个你可以依赖的人。

sentences.en: Now, vice versa, for the leader to know that they have highly skilled workers who are going to feel free to speak up
sentences.zh: 反过来，对领导来说，知道自己拥有高超技能的员工，并且他们有畅所欲言的安全感

sentences.en: when they have something to say and know what they're doing, dramatically lowers the stress level for the leader.
sentences.zh: 在有话要说时敢于表达且知道自己在做什么，会大大降低领导的压力水平。

sentences.en: It's obvious to me Dr. Corey Goldstein is good at his emergency medicine job and likes it.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，很显然科里·戈尔茨坦医生擅长他的急诊医学工作并且热爱它。

sentences.en: But even if a person loves what they do and works on a strong team, stress is still stress.
sentences.zh: 但即使一个人热爱自己的工作并在一个强大的团队中工作，压力依然是压力。

sentences.en: Psychologist Dennis Stolle says ongoing occupational stress can obviously burn some people out.
sentences.zh: 心理学家丹尼斯·施托尔表示，持续的职业压力显然会让一些人精疲力竭。

sentences.en: It is a situation where stress is unmanaged to the point that a person begins to experience emotional exhaustion and beginning to feel ineffective.
sentences.zh: 这种情况下的压力已经失控，以至于一个人开始感到情绪枯竭并开始觉得自己无能为力。

sentences.en: Oftentimes it may be there's so much work coming at me that nothing I can do will ever allow me to catch up.
sentences.zh: 通常情况可能是，有太多工作涌向我，我怎么做也无法赶上进度。

sentences.en: Stolle says unmanaged workplace burnout can have serious consequences for a person.
sentences.zh: 施托尔说，失控的职场职业倦怠会对个人产生严重的后果。

sentences.en: Chronic stress can lead to clinical depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 长期压力会导致临床抑郁症和焦虑症。

sentences.en: He says a protective tool for mental health is something called psychological capital.
sentences.zh: 他说，保护心理健康的一个工具有个名字叫心理资本。

sentences.en: That's different from psychological safety mentioned earlier.
sentences.zh: 这与前面提到的心理安全感不同。

sentences.en: Stolle says it's basically values a person can lean on during tough times.
sentences.zh: 施托尔说，这基本上是人在艰难时期可以依靠的价值观。

sentences.en: Psychological capital includes the elements of having hope and a sense of personal efficacy and resilience and optimism.
sentences.zh: 心理资本包括拥有希望、个人效能感、韧性以及乐观主义等元素。

sentences.en: One of the things that can actually make an individual begin to develop more psychological capital is by being around team members who already have a lot of psychological capital.
sentences.zh: 能让个人开始培养更多心理资本的方法之一，就是身处那些已经拥有大量心理资本的团队成员身边。

sentences.en: It's almost contagious in that sense.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，它几乎具有传染性。

sentences.en: So even if workers in high-stress jobs have all the protective factors we've heard about, psychological capital, being on a skilled team with strong leadership,
sentences.zh: 所以，即使身处高压工作的员工具备了我们所听到的所有保护因素，比如心理资本、身处拥有强大领导力的熟练团队中，

sentences.en: and having a healthy amount of psychological safety, is it really good for a person to work in this kind of high-pressure job day after day?
sentences.zh: 以及拥有健康的心理安全感，日复一日地在这样高压的岗位上工作对人真的好吗？

sentences.en: The American Psychological Association says employers can do all kinds of fundamental things to prevent workplace burnout,
sentences.zh: 美国心理协会表示，雇主可以采取各种根本性的措施来防止职场倦怠，

sentences.en: like make sure workers have realistic workloads and regular check-ins with their managers.
sentences.zh: 比如确保员工有现实的工作量以及与经理进行定期沟通。

sentences.en: Psychologist Dennis Stolle says one of the best things workplaces can offer their employees is vacation time.
sentences.zh: 心理学家丹尼斯·施托尔表示，职场能为员工提供的最好的事情之一就是休假时间。

sentences.en: The research is clear.
sentences.zh: 研究很明确。

sentences.en: Time away from work is essential.
sentences.zh: 远离工作的时间至关重要。

sentences.en: But it has to be a real break.
sentences.zh: 但必须是真正的休息。

sentences.en: It's not the vacation where you take your laptop and work from the beach.
sentences.zh: 那不是带着笔记本电脑在海滩上工作的度假。

sentences.en: That's not a vacation.
sentences.zh: 那不是度假。

sentences.en: It's actually taking time away from work.
sentences.zh: 那才是真正离开工作一段时间。

sentences.en: I followed up on this with Dr. Corey Goldstein at Rush University Medical Center in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 我为此跟进采访了芝加哥拉什大学医学中心的科里·戈尔茨坦医生。

sentences.en: He says he takes vacation time and has no problem disconnecting from the emergency department when he's out.
sentences.zh: 他说他会休假，而且在离开时可以毫无问题地切断与急诊室的联系。

sentences.en: He says working in emergency medicine gives him a certain perspective on stress in general.
sentences.zh: 他说从事急诊医学工作使他对整体压力有了一种特殊的看法。

sentences.en: A challenging shift can make the rest of his day feel pretty manageable.
sentences.zh: 具有挑战性的值班会让他一整天剩下的时间感觉相当容易应付。

sentences.en: For Call to Mind, I'm Jessica Bari in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 我是来自Call to Mind芝加哥站的杰西卡·巴里。

sentences.en: You're listening to The Strain of Stress, a special report from Call to Mind.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是Call to Mind的特别报道《压力的张力》。

sentences.en: I'm Angela Davis.
sentences.zh: 我是安吉拉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: As we just heard, taking time off from work is a great way to manage stress and prevent job burnout.
sentences.zh: 正如我们刚刚听到的，休假是管理压力和预防职业倦怠的好方法。

sentences.en: But it's just not possible for everyone to take a vacation.
sentences.zh: 但并不是每个人都能去度假。

sentences.en: And some of the factors that stress us are things we can't take a break from.
sentences.zh: 而且有些给我们造成压力的因素是我们无法抽身逃避的。

sentences.en: The research is clear.
sentences.zh: 研究很明确。

sentences.en: Stress is something that needs to be managed, and our mental health depends on it.
sentences.zh: 压力是需要管理的东西，我们的心理健康就靠它了。

sentences.en: Dr. Alyssa Eppel, who we heard from a bit ago, wrote a book called The Stress Prescription.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才听到的爱丽丝·埃佩尔医生写过一本书，叫做《压力处方》。

sentences.en: She shares science-backed tips that everyone can do to reduce stress in just minutes.
sentences.zh: 她分享了科学支持的技巧，每个人都可以在几分钟内做到减轻压力。

sentences.en: She suggests doing mindful check-ins, slowing down, breathing, and focusing on where you feel the stress in your body.
sentences.zh: 她建议进行正念打卡、放慢脚步、呼吸，并专注于你身体哪个部位感受到了压力。

sentences.en: Dr. Eppel also says nature is a powerful tool we just don't use enough.
sentences.zh: 埃佩尔医生还说，大自然是一个我们没有充分利用的强大工具。

sentences.en: Being outside to breathe fresh air and take in natural sounds and sights can turn down our stressful thoughts and make room to relax.
sentences.zh: 身处户外呼吸新鲜空气，倾听大自然的声音和景象，可以平息我们紧张的想法，为放松腾出空间。

sentences.en: Plus, nature is free, no prescription needed.
sentences.zh: 另外，大自然是免费的，无需处方。

sentences.en: When I spoke with Dr. Eppel, we also discussed how to handle all the uncertainty of stress.
sentences.zh: 当我与埃佩尔医生交谈时，我们还讨论了如何应对压力带来的所有不确定性。

sentences.en: I think a lot of what is stressing many people out right now is this feeling of, there's so much I can't control.
sentences.zh: 我想现在让许多人感到压力很大的很大一部分原因是这种感觉：有太多事情是我无法控制的。

sentences.en: I couldn't agree with you more.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意你的看法。

sentences.en: So if you think about what is bothering you most right now, it's very likely a situation where you don't have much control.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想想现在什么在最困扰你，那很可能是一个你无法掌控很多的局面。

sentences.en: And yet, our mind so easily creates a big stress response around that, even though we can't resolve the situation.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们的心很容易围绕这一点产生巨大的应激反应，尽管我们无法解决这种情况。

sentences.en: Once we recognize what we can and can't control, we can actually, what I call, drop the rope.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们认识到什么是我们能控制的，什么又是我们无法控制的，我们就可以真正做到我所说的“放下绳子”。

sentences.en: I suggest starting with thinking about one of the situations that you are carrying around that creates a lot of stress in your life.
sentences.zh: 我建议从思考你一直在承担的、给你的生活带来巨大压力的某种情况开始。

sentences.en: And asking yourself, how much of this situation do I control?
sentences.zh: 然后问问自己，这种情况有多少是我能控制的？

sentences.en: In many cases, there's very little.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，微乎其微。

sentences.en: And so in this moment, allowing ourselves to realize that we cannot solve it, that our mind may be problem solving, may be worrying,
sentences.zh: 所以在此时此刻，允许自己去意识到我们无法解决它，我们的大脑可能在解决问题，可能在担忧，

sentences.en: but that the most healthy thing we can do right now is to allow ourselves to put that down for now.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在能做的最健康的事情就是允许自己暂时放下它。

sentences.en: Those repeated experiences of letting go is one of our most important survival skills.
sentences.zh: 那些反复放手的经历是我们最重要的生存技能之一。

sentences.en: Just thinking about that makes me feel lighter.
sentences.zh: 光是想想这一点就让我觉得轻松多了。

sentences.en: Yes, and we might not even be aware that we're carrying them.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们甚至可能没有意识到我们在扛着它们。

sentences.en: So I like to picture us trying to pull on a boulder that can't move.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢想象我们在试图拉动一块无法移动的巨石。

sentences.en: And if we can then just say to ourselves, drop the rope and let yourself feel relief from all of that strain, that can be very powerful.
sentences.zh: 如果我们随后能对自己说，放下绳子，让自己从所有这些紧张中解脱出来，这会非常有力。

sentences.en: I say to myself, drop the rope several times a day.
sentences.zh: 我每天对自己说好几次“放下绳子”。

sentences.en: That was psychologist Alyssa Eppel from the University of California, San Francisco, and author of the book, The Stress Prescription.
sentences.zh: 那是来自加利福尼亚大学旧金山分校的心理学家爱丽丝·埃佩尔，她也是《压力处方》一书的作者。

sentences.en: I have to admit, these interviews and reports about stress have hit home for me.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，这些关于压力的采访和报道深深触动了我。

sentences.en: In August of 2025, a phone call from a nurse revealed I had breast cancer.
sentences.zh: 在2025年8月，一通护士打来的电话显示我得了乳腺癌。

sentences.en: My first response was, I don't have time for this.
sentences.zh: 我的第一反应是，我没时间应对这个。

sentences.en: I am already stressed.
sentences.zh: 我已经压力很大了。

sentences.en: I work full-time as a journalist, and much of the news is about division, uncertainty, and violence.
sentences.zh: 我全职从事新闻工作，大部分新闻都关于分裂、不确定性和暴力。

sentences.en: I'm a wife and the mother of two young adults who are navigating new jobs in cities far away from home.
sentences.zh: 我是一个妻子，也是两个年轻人的母亲，他们在远离家乡的城市里寻找新的工作。

sentences.en: I have high blood pressure.
sentences.zh: 我有高血压。

sentences.en: And now I have to handle a cancer diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 现在我还要应付癌症诊断？

sentences.en: Well, I learned I can handle it as long as I ask for help and use some of my coping skills.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我了解到只要我寻求帮助并运用我的一些应对技巧，我就能应付它。

sentences.en: Here's what works for me.
sentences.zh: 这是对我有用的方法。

sentences.en: Music.
sentences.zh: 音乐。

sentences.en: I listen to music a lot.
sentences.zh: 我经常听音乐。

sentences.en: For me, it's healing.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它能疗愈心灵。

sentences.en: I put together a recovery playlist when I was on leave of absence from work.
sentences.zh: 我在停薪留职期间制作了一份恢复播放列表。

sentences.en: Here's one of the songs I've been listening to repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 这是我一直在反复听的其中一首歌。

sentences.en: It's called Handle That.
sentences.zh: 这首歌叫《Handle That》。

sentences.en: And it's a collaboration by Artone, Simo, and FKA Jazz.
sentences.zh: 这是由 Artone、Simo 和 FKA Jazz 合作推出的。

sentences.en: Movement also helps me manage chronic stress.
sentences.zh: 运动也有助于我应对长期压力。

sentences.en: It does wonders.
sentences.zh: 效果非常神奇。

sentences.en: Going to the gym to walk on the elliptical machine or treadmill, then sitting in the steam sauna.
sentences.zh: 去健身房在椭圆机或跑步机上走走，然后去蒸汽桑拿房坐一坐。

sentences.en: It boosts my energy level and relaxes my mind.
sentences.zh: 它能提升我的精力并放松我的心灵。

sentences.en: Getting outdoors and taking in some fresh air has been powerful as well.
sentences.zh: 走到户外呼吸新鲜空气同样非常有效。

sentences.en: I also meet with a therapist every two weeks to talk about my worries and how setting boundaries can help me have more joy.
sentences.zh: 我每两周还去看一次心理治疗师，谈谈我的担忧，以及设定界限如何能帮我获得更多快乐。

sentences.en: I am now cancer-free, but I still deal with stress.
sentences.zh: 我现在已经战胜了癌症，但我仍然要面对压力。

sentences.en: The difference now is that I have a much better idea of how to drop the rope.
sentences.zh: 现在的区别在于，我更清楚该如何放手了。

sentences.en: You've been listening to The Strain of Stress, a special report from Call to Mind, American Public Media's initiative to foster new conversations about mental health.
sentences.zh: 您刚才收听的是《压力的负担》，这是一份来自“唤醒心灵”（Call to Mind）的特别报道，该项目是美国公共传媒（American Public Media）旨在促进关于心理健康全新对话的倡议。

sentences.zh: 本节目由我们的资深制作人杰西卡·巴里制作并撰稿，斯蒂芬·史密斯剪辑。

sentences.en: Our technical director is Alex Simpson, and Hans Butow scored the show.
sentences.zh: 我们的技术总监是亚历克斯·辛普森，汉斯·巴托为节目配乐。

sentences.zh: 感谢您收听《压力的负担》，这是“唤醒心灵”的一档特别报道。

sentences.zh: 这里是 APM，美国公共传媒。

sentences.zh: 如果您喜欢这个播客，请务必在您喜爱的播客应用中关注并订阅“唤醒心灵”，并给我们留下评价。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听。
